notes:
The Inbox: plug a card in with no project open
- With no project open, footage lands in the Inbox (a folder named Inbox beside your projects; an existing Loose Footage folder keeps being used). Auto mode can offload cards and take the global watch folder into it with nothing open.
- "File the Inbox…" on the Library page splits the Inbox into shoots (a new day, a gap of more than 3 hours, or what you said on camera) and files each into a new or existing project, moving the files into its folders (or leaving them in place if you untick Move). New projects get their Resolve project the way New Project makes it, without switching Resolve away from a project you have open.
- Say "this is the start of shoot 1" and "end of shoot 1" on camera and the split follows it.
- Auto-file the Inbox (Settings > Auto mode, Advanced, off by default) files each batch on its own once its analysis is done.
- Your agent can do the same over MCP: list_inbox, create_project and file_inbox_clips, and ingest_files takes inbox: true.
- Name it on the Library's "Footage with no name yet" rows now files that batch (it made an empty project before).

Crashes
- Pressing Done in Resync no longer crashes the app. A tool brought back from its chip never starts its work a second time, and closing a tool never takes down a worker that is still running.
- The face index and Fast describe no longer use the shared face detector at the same time (an access violation, and phantom "crowds" of 25 faces).
- A native fault the app survived is no longer reported as a crash on the next launch.

Faster and steadier analysis
- Time left is worked out from the minutes of footage left, not from how long the last few clips took, and says "estimating" until it knows.
- Analysis pauses itself and says why when the system drive is too full for the computer to grow its memory, instead of running into a freeze, and a clip that ran out of room is never counted as done.
- On the Mac, word timing is done in the same GPU pass; the CPU fallback waits until the lane is idle.
- Default skips clips the voice check heard nobody on, without decoding them again, and stops waiting for voice checks after 10 minutes.
- Sound files are never asked about as long clips.
- Rich describe no longer steps down below a size that is already loaded and working, holds instead of failing clip after clip when nothing fits, keeps "too slow" verdicts through a restart of the describe process, repairs a download missing its processor files, prices full precision when 4-bit cannot load, and never downloads inside the describe process.
- Dropping a folder the archive already analysed, or offloading a card you offloaded before, carries its analysis instead of running it all again.
- Ollama: its context is sized against what the app's own GPU lanes need on Windows too; unloads release the model actually in use; a cold start gets time to come up and its structuring is retried; downloads show real progress; Moondream's size is right and its download skips files the app never reads.
- Silent clips no longer get the transcription prompt saved as their transcript.

Sync and Resolve
- Audio sync never picks a camera without sound as the day's reference, prefers the camera that covers the most of the day, and re-picks for projects that got a silent reference.
- The Sync workspace reads MP3 and FLAC recordings, and long recordings no longer time out.
- Resync's waiting plan no longer pauses analysis, a second press brings it back, and with time-of-day placement off the plan no longer asks about placing clips.
- With the wrong Resolve project open, clips wait for the right one instead of failing, and the resume line says how many Resolve took.
- No more empty time-of-day timelines named after the project date. Missing-from-timeline warnings name the real reason.
- Metadata refresh only writes into the clip's own Resolve project.
- A slow Resolve start is "still starting", not "wedged", and no longer freezes the window every few seconds.

People, ingest and the rest
- A short Fast-describe look at a clip no longer replaces the People index's fuller one. Photos are indexed. Merges join people (not stale ids), keep the name, and Undo is visible.
- Catalog homes are planted at ingest for custom footage folder names, never nested inside another catalog.
- Sony AVF_INFO and recorder temp files stay on the card; our own .md sidecars are not loose documents.
- Several GUI-thread stalls are gone (stand-down tick, Ollama checks, brain switcher, footprint sampling, media band, queue tab), and the brain switcher no longer shrinks the main window.
- "All caught up" and "Everything is written" are never said while clips still owe a description.
- Valid DJI start timecodes are read at the timecode track's own rate.
- Smaller honest-wording fixes across the queue, the dial's reasons, the AI rough cut's advice, apply reports, the update dialog (X and Esc now cancel the download) and HELP.
